blocks.text: Fear stayed high, but the space started calling for a "generational entry"

Nobody opens CT hoping to read “I don’t know”. They want someone to blame or somebody who sounds certain enough to borrow from for a minute. This week, that certainty kept moving from one explanation to the next, while being right tomorrow remained optional 🤪

Early in the week, BTC fell into the mid-55Ks and Fear & Greed stayed in Extreme Fear. By Thursday, BTC had recovered toward $60K to $61K, but the mood didn’t recover in a straight line. First came capitulation posts; then the bounce gave people an opening to call the bottom.
Kaleo called the dip the start of a “golden bull run”
while Ash Crypto compared current conditions to the 2022 bottom:
Astronomer talked about next cycle upside while defending the bottom thesis.
Price wise, even with BTC recovering toward $60K the supposed 'entry zone' stretched down to $52K. But some traders had confidence in the long term case.
Saylor stayed with his usual buy and hold message and a P Morgan comment about the bottom being in gave people another line to read as confirmation 🥸
Miner capitulation posts also got used to support the bottom call. That may fit the argument, but it doesn’t settle it.
"Buy the dip" discussions didn’t mean everyone had stopped worrying about the market:

U.S. spot BTC and ETH ETFs continued to see outflows, crypto remained tied to other risk assets and the $7.4 billion options expiry scheduled for tomorrow was still the near term event traders were watching.
Bitcoin and macro took up plenty of attention, but they weren’t the only stories holding on.
AI agents remained one of CT’s stronger non price topics, with related tokens showing relative strength while the wider market struggled.

Solana memes and Robinhood linked tokens kept the speculative side active. RWA discussions, by contrast, cooled off from previous weeks. A real change in attention this week, though it doesn’t mean the underlying interest in tokenized assets has disappeared.
Around Nov 24–25 a wallet linked to Ansem sold a large amount of $ANSEM (reports of ~$1.5M), sending the token from ~$36M to ~$10M.
He claimed it was a hack. Large parts of CT did not buy it and treated it as a dump/rug or inside job. The token later recovered some ground, but the trust damage and callout posts stayed active.

Thanksgiving added its own layer to the mood. Posts comparing this year’s performance with previous Thanksgivings pointed out how little BTC had gained on average over the past five years. It was a grim seasonal comparison, and it fit the week better than the “golden bull run” calls did.
Engagement was lower than usual, partly because of the U.S. holiday, so the conversation stayed concentrated around price, bottom calls and the tokens still attracting speculation 🥱
If we had to invent a metric on the spot and call it CT Pulse, we'd put this week at 5/10. The main discussions kept going, but holiday week engagement kept the meter from climbing much higher.
